key_insight: Neural operator surrogates can replace expensive CFD solves inside Bayesian MCMC inverse design while preserving posterior geometry and uncertainty structure.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical uncertainty-aware aerodynamic inverse design with orders-of-magnitude faster turnaround, making Bayesian CFD workflows more usable for design optimization and decision-making.
method: Formulate Bayesian inverse design for quasi-1D nozzle flow using sparse flow observations and geometry priors.
Replace the CFD solver with a Deep Operator Network inside a No-U-Turn Sampler while keeping the likelihood, priors, and sampling settings fixed.
Compare a surrogate-based posterior against the CFD reference and also test a direct inverse neural operator for single-shot reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Across sparse to fully observed regimes, the surrogate reproduces posterior geometry and uncertainty trends of the CFD baseline while reducing total inference time to under one second, exceeding a three-order-of-magnitude speedup.
watch_item: Posterior quality depends strongly on geometry parameterization, so surrogate acceleration may still fail or become misleading if the inverse problem is poorly conditioned or shock-dominated flows are not well represented.
paper_title: Accelerating Bayesian inverse design in computational fluid dynamics using neural operators
